battle.name: 十王會戰
battle.theater: 赫拉克勒奧波利斯至底比斯河段
battle.brief: 十王會戰是埃及第一中間期末年南方底比斯與中埃及赫拉克勒奧波利斯爭奪「兩地之王」名分的衝突，在《棺銘》中被寫成諸神率十位北方王交戰的神話段落。步兵以銅矛為制式裝備，方陣以矛葉橫列抵禦衝撞，弓手在後列拋射；戰爭列表把此戰繫於前1400年，實際歷史核心則在前2200年至前2050年間。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 本場戰爭的交戰方，一方是尼羅河谷南方的底比斯王權，一方是佔據中埃及的赫拉克勒奧波利斯王權，兩邊都以「上下埃及之王」的名號互相排斥；此外還有第三支力量，即《棺銘》敘事中與人間軍隊並列的「諸神」。底比斯一方以瓦塞特（今盧克索）為都，當時第十一王朝初期才脫離阿拜多斯王墓圈，實控範圍只在南埃及，軍隊以埃及語所稱的 nfswt（步兵民兵）為骨架，徵召自地方氏族的長矛兵與弓手，另有靠尼羅河南段、與象島一線船廠相連的運兵與糧食船隊。赫拉克勒奧波利斯一方以伊赫納西亞·梅勒迪納特（今米尼亞省伊布謝克）為都，自第九王朝起統治中埃及，並握有靠近北方戰線的渡口與運河樞紐，其軍隊同樣以步兵方陣與弓手為主，並可從尼羅河三角洲與中埃及沿岸抽調人力。敘事裡的「十王」指的就是這條北方王朝線上的王統，而不是十支互不相同的軍隊；學者亦常把「十王」解讀為赫拉克勒奧波利斯諸王加上三角洲與綠洲一帶的地方首領。雙方都不靠車馬作戰：戰車要到第二中間期、隨喜克索斯人進入埃及才出現，與本場衝突的年代相隔數百年。
countriesEn: The two sides in this war were the Theban kingship in the south of the Nile valley and the Herakleopolitan kingship in Middle Egypt, and each of them claimed the title of king of Upper and Lower Egypt in a way that excluded the other. A third force stands alongside the human armies in the narrative of the Coffin Texts, and that is the gods themselves. The Theban side had its capital at Waset, modern Luxor; the Eleventh Dynasty had only just detached itself from the royal necropolis at Abydos, and its effective territory covered the south of Egypt alone. Its army rested on the nfswt, the Egyptian term for the foot soldier mustered as a levy, with spearmen and bowmen drawn from the local clans, backed by a river fleet of troop and grain boats reaching down the Nile to the yards of Elephantine. The Herakleopolitan side had its capital at Ihnasya el-Medinat, modern Ibsheq in Minya governorate; it had ruled Middle Egypt since the Ninth Dynasty and held the crossings and the canal junctions closest to the northern front, with an army built in the same way out of infantry squares and bowmen, and able to draw men from the Delta and from the Middle Egyptian riverbank. The ten kings of the narrative are the royal line of that northern dynasty, not ten separate armies; scholars commonly read the ten as the Herakleopolitan kings together with the local chiefs of the Delta and of the oasis. Neither side fought from chariots: the chariot did not reach Egypt until the Second Intermediate Period, with the Hyksos, centuries after the conflict recorded here.
people: 留下姓名的有兩類人。一類是底比斯的王：英提夫一世在阿拜多斯王墓圈起兵，把「底比斯」變成獨立的王號；英提夫二世延續北征，在薩卡拉為家族所建的墳墓（TT386）留下自述，提到自己與北方敵人以及「沙漠居民」的交鋒，這段銘文是本場衝突最接近第一手的一份材料；英提夫三世守住瓦塞特的基地，門提赫特普二世則在約前2050年前後完成對全埃及的整合。戰爭列表把本場繫於前1400年一帶的舊王國末段，與上述王朝的實際年代相隔數百年，引用時須分清傳統繫年與史實年代。另一類是赫拉克勒奧波利斯一方的王：尼斐爾卡拉、梅里卡拉等名見於殘存的王名圈、印章與王室墓地，馬內托留下的王表把第九王朝記作八王、第十王朝記作十九王，遠多於考古可證的數目，這種落差本身就說明北方那條王統的記錄在傳抄中散佚嚴重。還有一位身分在文字中始終不明的人物，在中王國的《教誨書》中以亡王口吻現身：他自述曾平定外來侵者、令赫拉克勒奧波利斯歸順，又在圍攻該城時遭親信暗殺，臨終勸兒子不要輕信任何一人。棺銘裡的「我」則是尚未稱王的先王或王儲，自稱與神同行、參與了對北方十王的戰鬥。
peopleEn: Two kinds of name survive. The first are the kings of Thebes: Intef I raised his standard in the royal necropolis at Abydos and turned Thebes into a capital in its own right; Intef II carried the northern war on, and left an autobiography in the family tomb he built for himself at Saqqara (TT386), where he speaks of clashes with the enemy of the north and with the desert dwellers. That inscription is the closest thing to a first-hand account of this conflict. Intef III held the base at Waset, and Mentuhotep II completed the integration of the whole of Egypt around 2050 BC. The war list ties this battle to around 1400 BC in the closing phase of the Old Kingdom, several centuries away from the actual dates of those dynasties, and the two have to be kept apart. The second kind of name belongs to the kings of Herakleopolis: Neferkare, Merikare and others appear in surviving cartouches, seals and royal tombs, while the king list of Manetho counts the Ninth Dynasty at eight kings and the Tenth at nineteen, far more than archaeology can confirm; that gap in itself shows how badly the records of the northern line were scattered as they were copied. One further person appears without a name of his own, speaking in the voice of a dead king in the Middle Kingdom Instructions of Amenemhat: he tells how he had put down foreign invaders and brought Herakleopolis to order, and how he was murdered by his own intimates while besieging that city, and on his deathbed warns his son to trust no one at all. The 'I' of the Coffin Texts is a king or an heir not yet on the throne, claiming to have travelled with the gods and to have taken part in the battle against the ten kings of the north.
kits: 本卡的埃及長矛是早王朝以來沿用的制式近戰兵器：銅或青銅矛頭綁在木桿上，結構簡單、可以量產，正好支撐以步兵方陣為核心的埃及軍隊。從第一中間期一路到中王國早期，這種矛仍是埃及士兵的主要兵器，近身時以矛葉橫掃與直刺對付對方的劍與斧，遠處則靠弓手的箭雨。同一時期可以對照的形制有幾種：單刃前彎的科普什式短劍仍是軍官與近衛的標誌性兵器；銅刃戰斧握在有產者手中；矛有單葉、雙葉與三叉等不同樣式；防護靠皮或木框的小圓盾，護身多為皮背銅片，富裕者才穿整片銅鎧。投射武器是自製木弓與箭，早期弓只有兩三股筋腱，沒有複合弓；投擲棒則是獵人與步兵都會帶的便攜武器。沒有戰車：這類車輛要到第二中間期才出現於埃及，最早的實例來自喜克索斯人。補給與運輸倚賴尼羅河，重船由岸上人力拖行，牛拉橇車負責陸運，船隊把穀物運到前線，也把軍隊送往上游。攻城沒有成熟的攻城塔與撞槌，主要手段是封鎖渡口、切斷糧道與長期圍困泥磚築成的赫拉克勒奧波利斯。
kitsEn: The Egyptian spear on this card is a standard weapon of close combat carried over from the Early Dynastic period: a copper or bronze head bound to a wooden shaft, simple in construction and capable of being produced in quantity, which is exactly what an Egyptian army built around infantry squares needed. From the First Intermediate Period through the early Middle Kingdom this spear remained the main weapon of the Egyptian soldier; at close quarters the blade was swung and thrust against the enemy's sword and axe, and at range the work was done by the archers' arrows. Several other forms of the same period can be set beside it: the single-edged, forward-curving khopesh-type short sword remained the badge of officers and of the royal guard; the bronze-bladed battle axe belonged to those who could afford one; spears existed in single-leaf, double-leaf and trident forms; protection came from small round shields of hide or wood over a frame, and from leather armour backed with bronze scales, only the richer wearing solid bronze. The missile weapon was a self bow of wood with its own arrows, the early bow carrying only two or three strands of sinew, with no composite bow anywhere; the throwing stick was the portable weapon carried by hunters and by soldiers alike. There were no chariots: the vehicle did not appear in Egypt until the Second Intermediate Period, and its earliest instances came with the Hyksos. Supply and movement depended on the Nile: the heavy boats were towed from the bank by men on foot, cattle-drawn sledges handled the land transport, and the fleets carried grain forward to the front and the army upstream. For siege there was no mature tower or battering ram; the methods were to seal the crossings, cut the grain road and besiege the mudbrick city of Herakleopolis for a long time.
tactics: 底比斯的打法建立在尼羅河的地形上。河谷是一條狹長走廊，東岸是通往紅海的丘陵，西岸是通往利比亞的開闊地，誰控制高地與渡口，誰就控制南北交通。底比斯人的第一步是把軍隊與船隊一起沿河北上，步兵沿東岸行軍，弓手在縱隊之前展開搜索水源與偵察敵情，船隊在後方把糧食跟上，遇汛期水漲便靠岸駐紮。接近敵陣之後，埃及式的密集步兵方陣展開：前列長矛手把矛葉朝前排成一線，用以頂住對方的衝撞；弓手在後方以拋射的箭壓制；軍官與王家親兵在陣前指揮，少數馬匹用於偵察與追擊，並不成建制騎兵。對赫拉克勒奧波利斯的攻勢則是持久戰：先奪取三角洲方向的渡口與運河節點，使北方城市失去糧源，然後以圍城消耗，逼其求和或內訌；北方陣營裡因饑荒與戰敗而北逃的氏族，被底比斯收編安置，成為自己軍隊的一部分。《棺銘》的敘事把同一套邏輯寫成神話：神的船隊同行，戰士以長矛與弓作戰，北方十王的聯軍潰散，死者因參戰而得到「使兩地重歸生計」的名分。
tacticsEn: The Theban method was built on the geography of the Nile. The valley is a long narrow corridor, with hills running towards the Red Sea on the east bank and open ground towards Libya on the west; whoever holds the heights and the crossings controls the traffic between north and south. The first step for the Thebans was to move army and fleet north together, infantry marching along the eastern bank, bowmen spreading out ahead of the column to find water and read the enemy's movements, while the fleet brought the grain on behind and pulled in to the bank when the flood rose. On closing with the enemy the Egyptian dense infantry square opened out: the spearmen in the front rank levelled their blades in a single line to hold off the impact, the bowmen behind them kept up the pressure with their arrows, and officers with the king's own guard commanded from the front; the few horses were used for scouting and for pursuit and did not amount to a cavalry arm. The offensive against Herakleopolis was a war of endurance: first the crossings and the canal junctions in the direction of the Delta were taken, cutting the grain off from the northern cities, and then the siege was allowed to grind them down into seeking terms or into quarrelling among themselves; clans who fled north out of the northern camp, hungry and beaten, were taken in and resettled by the Thebans and became part of their own force. The narrative of the Coffin Texts writes the same logic as myth: the boat of the gods sails in company, the fighters use spear and bow, the league of the ten northern kings breaks up, and the dead man who fought in it earns the title of 'the one who makes the two lands live again'.
data: 可以核對的數字不多，但有幾個支點。第一是「十」：文本所指的北方統治者恰為十位，這個數目很可能來自對一串已知王名的概括，學界因此把它與赫拉克勒奧波利斯王朝的實際君主數掛鈎；馬內托留下的是第九王朝八王、第十王朝十九王的表，合計二十七，但考古可確證姓名的只有八到九位左右。第二是年代：第一中間期一般定在約前2200年至前2050年之間，底比斯完成統一多被放在約前2050年；戰爭列表把本場繫於前1400年，屬於後世編年框架的傳統定位，與這段神話所保存的歷史記憶並不重合。第三是距離：伊赫納西亞·梅勒迪納特到瓦塞特沿河約三百公里上下，迂迴陸路更遠，冬季低水位會讓淺灘難以通行，軍隊只能在少數幾處渡口過河。第四是兵器尺度：早王朝的銅矛頭長約十五至二十五公分，木桿約一點五至二公尺，重量輕到可以單手持握並連續刺擊，這是它能成為步兵制式裝備的物理原因。第五是文本體量：《棺銘》中處理這場戰爭的段落，是整套文獻中少數以連貫敘事出現的部分，而不是一句咒語。文本本身沒有留下月日，卡上所記的第四月是按埃及曆的行軍季節推定的，水位回落、河谷可通行，北方遠征多在涼季展開。
dataEn: There are not many figures that can be checked, but there are a few anchors. The first is the ten: the narrative names exactly ten rulers of the north, and that number most likely comes from a generalisation over a list of known royal names, which is why scholars connect it with the actual number of kings of the Herakleopolitan dynasty; the table of Manetho gives eight kings for the Ninth Dynasty and nineteen for the Tenth, twenty-seven in all, whereas only eight or nine names can be confirmed archaeologically. The second is date: the First Intermediate Period is generally placed between about 2200 and 2050 BC, and the reunification of Egypt by Thebes is usually put at about 2050 BC; the war list ties this battle to 1400 BC, which is a traditional placement in a later chronological frame and does not coincide with the historical memory preserved by the myth. The third is distance: from Ihnasya el-Medinat to Waset is about three hundred kilometres by river and further by the circuitous land route, and at low water in winter the shallows become impassable, so an army could cross only at a handful of fords. The fourth is the scale of the weapon: the copper spearhead of the Early Dynastic period is about fifteen to twenty-five centimetres long, on a shaft of roughly one and a half to two metres, light enough to be held one-handed and thrust repeatedly, which is the physical reason it could become standard infantry kit. The fifth is the bulk of the text: the passage in the Coffin Texts that deals with this battle is one of the few parts of that literature written as continuous narrative rather than as a single spell. The text itself carries no month and no day; the fourth month recorded with the card is inferred from the campaigning season of the Egyptian calendar, when the water has fallen, the valley is passable and northern expeditions are normally undertaken in the cool part of the year.
cause: 打起來的直接背景是中央權力的崩解。舊王國末期，尼羅河的氾濫與反覆的旱災讓耕地面積縮減，饑荒從三角洲蔓延到中埃及，稅基與兵源大量流失，位於尼羅河中游的赫拉克勒奧波利斯一系趁勢取得獨立的王權，並在稅收與軍隊上與南方的底比斯王權形成兩套彼此否定的秩序：兩邊都自稱「上下埃及之王」，北線與南線沿河相望，誰都不能容忍對方坐穩。底比斯的動機很直接：英提夫一世把王號立在瓦塞特，等於宣告脫離北方的宗主；英提夫二世北上，就是要把赫拉克勒奧波利斯的勢力從中埃及趕走，把北界推回尼羅河三角洲。他的家族墳墓自述提到他對北方敵人與沙漠居民作戰，說明南方的目標不只是一座城，而是一整條北岸的進取線。赫拉克勒奧波利斯一方則必須守住中埃及這一段河谷，失去它就失去了一半的稅源與兵源。文本層面，這場衝突還有另一重原因：棺銘把北方王寫成混沌的代理人，把戰爭解釋成秩序與混亂的對抗，讓戰神的形象在死後仍然延續；對一位尚未取得全埃及的南方王來說，神話是最省成本的合法性來源。
causeEn: The immediate background to the fighting was the collapse of central authority. In the closing phase of the Old Kingdom the Nile's inundations and recurring droughts shrank the area under cultivation, famine spread from the Delta into Middle Egypt, and the tax base and the manpower drained away. The line of Herakleopolis, sitting in the middle reaches of the river, used the opening to take an independent kingship of its own and set up two mutually negating orders of taxation and armies against the Theban kingship in the south: both claimed to be king of Upper and Lower Egypt, the northern and the southern lines faced each other along the river, and neither could tolerate the other consolidating its position. The Theban motive is plain. Intef I set up his royal title at Waset, which was a declaration of independence from the northern overlord; Intef II marched north to drive the Herakleopolitan interest out of Middle Egypt and to push the northern frontier back to the Delta. The autobiography in his family tomb speaks of his fighting the enemy of the north and the desert dwellers, which shows that the southern aim was not one city but a whole line of advance along the north bank. The Herakleopolitan side had to hold the Middle Egyptian stretch of the valley, because losing it meant losing half its revenue and half its recruits. At the level of the text the conflict had a second cause as well: the Coffin Texts make the northern kings agents of chaos and turn the war into a confrontation between order and chaos, so that the warrior's divine identity outlives his death. For a southern king who did not yet hold all Egypt, that myth was the least expensive source of legitimacy available.
impact: 這場戰爭最深遠的後果，是埃及從此擺脫第一中間期的分裂，重新變成一個有單一王權的國家。赫拉克勒奧波利斯的王室一系中斷，中埃及的行政與宗教重心往南移，隨後在阿斯尤特一帶出現的地方藝術風格，反映舊秩序崩解與新中心整合的過程。更大的影響在觀念層面：把北方王的失敗寫成神的參與，使「王」在文學中被寫成半神半人的存在，戰鬥者與神的戰鬥並列，這種寫法在往後中王國與新王國的棺材銘與神廟文本裡不斷被複製，塑造了埃及王權的自我形象：法老是神在人間的執行者，戰爭不是兩套權力的算式，而是秩序對混亂的一次具體勝利。反過來說，《教誨書》那類文本所散發的疑心——對親信、對政敵、對人倫都不能全然信任——也構成中王國政治文化的底色，推動了中央集權、專職官僚與固定軍隊的形成。考古層面，赫拉克勒奧波利斯發現的兩座王陵金字塔與王室墓地是埃及現存最北端的金字塔，底比斯方面則留下英提夫家族的合葬墳墓；兩地的器物、封泥與王名圈，構成本場戰爭目前唯一的物質證據。
impactEn: The deepest consequence of this war was that Egypt came out of the fragmentation of the First Intermediate Period and became once more a country with a single kingship. The royal line of Herakleopolis was cut off, the administrative and religious centre of Middle Egypt shifted southward, and the local artistic style that appeared around Asyut afterwards reflects both the break-up of the old order and the process of a new centre being welded together. The greater effect lies in the realm of ideas. Writing the defeat of the northern kings as an act of the gods made the king in literature into a being half divine and half human, with the warrior set alongside the fighting of the gods; that way of writing was copied again and again in the coffin texts and the temple texts of the later Middle and New Kingdoms, and it shaped the Egyptian royal image of itself: the pharaoh is the god's instrument on earth, and war is not the arithmetic of two powers but a concrete victory of order over chaos. Read the other way round, the mistrust that texts like the Instructions of Amenemhat radiate — towards close associates, towards rivals, towards human relations in general — became a foundation of Middle Kingdom political culture and pushed the state towards centralisation, a professional bureaucracy and a standing army. Archaeologically, the two royal pyramids and the royal necropolis found at Herakleopolis are the northernmost pyramids in Egypt to survive, while Thebes has left the joint family tomb of the Intef family; the objects, the sealings and the cartouches from both sites are the only material evidence for this war that we have.
result: 打到最後，站在河谷中段的是底比斯。赫拉克勒奧波利斯王朝的統治中斷，北方王統在文獻中不再延續，中埃及的城鎮與渡口重新編入以瓦塞特為中心的秩序，約前2050年前後上下埃及統一，隨後第十二王朝以孟斐斯為新的行政中心，尼羅河谷恢復由單一王權調度的軍隊與稅制。《棺銘》的敘事則給了這場戰爭另一個結局：十位北方王全部潰散，戰勝者不是凡人，而是與神同行的軍隊；死者被寫成「使兩地重歸生計」的人，並且在身後獲得與神同乘的船。換句話說，歷史上的結果是北方王室的消失與埃及的重新統一，文學上的結果是王權被神化。兩者之間也留著一段縫隙：赫拉克勒奧波利斯諸王的姓名、卒年與下場，至今大多無從確認，輸的一方在史冊上只剩下「十王」這個數目。對底比斯自己而言，統一不是終點：門提赫特普二世之後，南王朝很快進入第十二王朝的整頓期，把北方的空缺收編成新的編制，而這段記憶則被寫進往後每一代王的自我敘述裡，成為「統一者」這一名號的來源。
resultEn: In the end Thebes stood in the middle reaches of the valley. The rule of the Herakleopolitan dynasty was broken, the northern royal line no longer continues in the documents, the towns and the crossings of Middle Egypt were folded back into an order centred on Waset, and Upper and Lower Egypt were reunited at about 2050 BC; the Twelfth Dynasty then made Memphis its new administrative centre, and the Nile valley returned to a single authority directing its armies and its taxes. The narrative of the Coffin Texts gives the same war a second ending: all ten northern kings are routed, and the victors are not mortals but an army that travels with the gods; the dead man is written down as 'the one who makes the two lands live again' and is granted a boat to sail with the gods after death. In other words, the historical result was the disappearance of the northern royal house and the reunification of Egypt, while the literary result was the deification of kingship. A gap remains between the two: the names, the dates of death and the fates of the Herakleopolitan kings can for the most part no longer be established, and the losing side survives in the historical record as nothing more than the number ten. For Thebes itself, unity was not an ending. After Mentuhotep II the southern dynasty moved into the reorganisation of the Twelfth Dynasty, converting the northern vacancy into new administrative units, and the memory of the war was written into the self-portrait of every later king, becoming the source of that title of 'the one who unites'.
